status_summary: EO 14192 (signed 2025-01-31) directed the Treasury Secretary and the OMB Director to reinstate the April 2018 Treasury and OMB memorandum of agreement on tax regulation review; a tax advisory summary describes the 2023 agreement it displaced as having again exempted tax regulations. A Treasury and OMB memorandum of agreement dated 2025-07-04, whose terms are known through a browser retrieval of a scanned file, provides for OIRA review of tax regulatory actions that may create a serious inconsistency with another agency's action, raise novel legal or policy issues, or have an annual non-revenue effect of 100 million dollars or more, with reviews generally concluding 45 days after OIRA receives the required information, an expedited track of up to 10 business days for implementing H.R. 1, exemptions for categories such as OFAC sanctions rules and CFIUS rules, and supersession of the 1983 agreement and rescission of the 2023-06-09 agreement. In March 2026 one IRS proposed rule was designated for OIRA review as significant under the agreement, while another final rule was recorded as not subject to review. The arrangement is an executive agreement that can be changed.

timeline.event: EO 14192 signed, directing reinstatement of the 2018 Treasury and OMB tax regulation review agreement.

Treasury and OMB sign a memorandum of agreement on review of tax regulations under EO 12866: OIRA reviews actions meeting one of three triggers (inconsistency with another agency, novel issues, annual non-revenue effect of 100 million dollars or more), with a 45-day review norm and a 10-business-day expedited track for implementing H.R. 1; it supersedes the 1983 agreement and rescinds the 2023-06-09 agreement.

timeline.event: An IRS proposed rule stated it was designated for OIRA review and classified significant under the 2025 agreement.

title: Keep Treasury tax regulations under OIRA review
uncertainties: The 2025 agreement was read through a browser retrieval supplied to the project and was not opened in readable form by the research tools or by the independent reviewers: direct fetches of the Treasury PDF returned only its date line because the file is a scan, and on 2026-10-18 a further fetch again returned only the date while a direct download was refused by the network gateway, so its terms rest on that retrieval. The typed name of the Treasury signer is partly illegible in the scan. The document does not mention the 2018 agreement, so whether the 2025 terms match the 2018 terms the recommendation refers to was not compared, and the record cannot say that the 2018 agreement was reinstated as such. The recommendation text describes the 2018 agreement and gives no thresholds of its own. Review is limited to actions meeting the three triggers and excludes listed categories, which is narrower than review of every tax regulatory action. The proportion of tax rules actually sent to OIRA was not measured. The statement about the 2023 agreement's effect rests on one tax advisory summary.
